$comment: Hand-curated search aliases. Source, not generated: edit this file. Read by lib/icon-taxonomy.ts for the site and by pipeline/build-data.mjs for the packages, which is why it is JSON rather than a TypeScript literal.

aliases.note: Families.

The plural as a concept: every drawing carrying more than one arrowhead, which is the question `arrows` is asking and the one word the name of each of these does not answer. Counted off the drawings rather than the names: `maximize` and `minimize` are corner brackets with no arrow in them, `fast-forward`, `rewind` and `skip-*` are play heads, and `rotate-ccw` and `rotate-cw` carry exactly one. `arrows` is held apart from `arrow` by the singular rule, which leaves it alone, so the two words stay two questions.
The CC form. `subtitles` is the same idea drawn as caption lines.
Named for its base, but it is also the add-to-queue mark.

Figma's description spells these `log out` and `log in`, which reaches `LogOut` because the identifier splits into two words, and misses `logout` typed as one. The closed-up forms are what people type.

Figma's description spells these `log out` and `log in`, which reaches `LogOut` because the identifier splits into two words, and misses `logout` typed as one. The closed-up forms are what people type.
Both angle-bracket icons, plus the markup words only the second one earns. `terminal` already answers to "code", so these join a word the set has.
The family, so every member answers to these.
Named columns x rows. There is no bare `grid`: the word said nothing about which one, and it reaches the family through the name anyway.
Base-first like every compound here, and `heart` is the base that actually exists. `hand heart` is the word order people arrive with.
The family, so repeat-1 answers to these too.
The theme toggle is why anyone reaches for either of these in an app, and neither drawing is named after it.
The bulb is reached for as an idea, not as a lamp.
Modifiers, which compose with whatever they hang off.
The error mark, which is what a toast reaches for. `stop` is the sign the shape comes from.
The words for what it does. Nobody types `grip` first.
The words for what it holds, and the two names other sets use.
`spanner` is what half the world calls it, and nobody types `wrench` looking for settings.
A grid of shapes reads as a group or a selection long before anyone types its drawing.
The knob form, against the plain `sliders-*` equaliser: the thumb is what people are looking for.
Nobody types `ban` for the sign; they type what it means.
Nobody types the compound name; they type what they are doing with it.
Two rings that cross: the drawing is the overlap, so the words are about the overlap. "ring" lives here rather than in the filename, which says circle like the other 73.
The dashed ring is the one that is not there yet, so the words are about the pending half.
Not a square in a circle: a ring and a rounded square crossing. Listed in lib/icon-not-containers.json for that reason.
Same pair as circle-square with the square left dashed.
The software sense outweighs the wall socket: this is what an integration is drawn with.
The family, so the signs inherit it.
The plain flag: a marker, a report and a milestone. The chequered one has its own row.
The magnifier with a plus: zoom in, and add-to-search.
Results, rather than the act of searching.
The finish line, not a country.
The sign is inside the cloud, so these read as the state of a sync rather than of a file.
Only the two that say something went wrong carry the failure words; a synced or added cloud is not an error.
The sign is on the parcel's own corner, so these read as the state of an order rather than of a file.
No bare `app`: the tile is `square`, and only the badged members carry the word.
wifi-exclamation is the one icon that spells this mark the other way, so the word it uses has to find the rest.
What people type for a form they fill in: 2 empty searches for survey in the first month.
The words a learner types: lesson, skill and study were empty searches before the shelf existed.
Analysis and analytics are the words for a chart someone has not named yet.
Budget, asset, bank and acct all came in empty; money words, not card words.
Reward and redemption vocabulary: every one of these was an empty search.
A platform mark, not the fruit: it sits on the download button that hands a Mac its own build.
Drawn for the reference surface behind a feature: the manual, the guide, the legend beside a diagram. `book` is on the name already.
Drawn for the shortcut hint, which is what most interfaces reach for a keyboard to say. The words for the device itself are on the name.
The verb: pinned in place, kept at the top. `map-pin` is the place marker and has its own row.
The other half of the download pair.

$names: Names other sets use for a drawing here, keyed by the drawing. Matched against the whole query, never split into words: these are names, not keywords, and folding `message-square` into a keyword list makes a search for `square` return every message icon.
